Package dev.itsharshxd.zentrix.api.cosmetics

Interface CosmeticHandler

public interface CosmeticHandler
What an addon implements for a cosmetic type it registers with CosmeticsService.registerType(org.bukkit.plugin.Plugin, dev.itsharshxd.zentrix.api.cosmetics.CosmeticTypeDefinition, dev.itsharshxd.zentrix.api.cosmetics.CosmeticHandler): the cosmetics there are, and what they do.

Zentrix does the rest as it does for its own categories: it stores who owns and chose what, lists the type in /cosmetics, checks permissions, sells cosmetics that have a price, and calls this handler when one of them should show.

Every method is called on the main thread. One that throws is logged and skipped, so a failing handler cannot break a match or a menu. 


 public final class HatHandler implements CosmeticHandler {
     public List<CosmeticDefinition> getCosmetics() {
         return hats.values().stream().map(Hat::definition).toList();
     }

     public void onTrigger(CosmeticTrigger trigger) {
         switch (trigger.moment()) {
             case GAME_START -> wear(trigger.player(), trigger.cosmetic().getId());
             case GAME_LEAVE -> takeOff(trigger.player());
             default -> { }
         }
     }

     public boolean startPreview(Player player, CosmeticDefinition cosmetic, Runnable onFinish) {
         wear(player, cosmetic.getId());
         Bukkit.getScheduler().runTaskLater(plugin, () -> {
             takeOff(player);
             onFinish.run();
         }, 100L);
         return true;
     }
 }

  • Method Details

    • getCosmetics

      @NotNull @NotNull List<CosmeticDefinition> getCosmetics()
      Every cosmetic of the type, in the order menus list them. Asked whenever Zentrix needs them, so a reload of the addon's own configuration shows at once; keep it quick.

      A cosmetic removed from the list stays owned by those who own it, and counts again once it is listed again. IDs must be unique; a repeated one is ignored.

    • onTrigger

      default void onTrigger(@NotNull @NotNull CosmeticTrigger trigger)
      A player's equipped cosmetic of this type, triggered at one of the moments the type's definition lists. A CosmeticTriggerEvent listener may have skipped it.

    • onEquippedChange

      default void onEquippedChange(@NotNull @NotNull org.bukkit.entity.Player player, @Nullable @Nullable CosmeticDefinition equipped)
      What an online player has equipped of this type changed: they chose another, it was taken away or expired, or their cosmetics were read as they joined. For a cosmetic that shows outside matches, such as in the lobby. Not called as players leave the server.
      Parameters:
      equipped - the cosmetic now in effect, or null when there is none

    • startPreview

      default boolean startPreview(@NotNull @NotNull org.bukkit.entity.Player player, @NotNull @NotNull CosmeticDefinition cosmetic, @NotNull @NotNull Runnable onFinish)
      Shows a cosmetic to a player for a while, as the cosmetics menu's right-click does. Zentrix closes the menu first and opens it again once onFinish runs.
      Parameters:
      onFinish - to run once the preview has finished on its own; not after stopPreview(org.bukkit.entity.Player)
      Returns:
      whether it shows; false, the default, when this type has no previews

    • stopPreview

      default void stopPreview(@NotNull @NotNull org.bukkit.entity.Player player)
      Ends a player's preview early: they started another, left, or an addon asked. Called only while a preview this handler started has not finished.

    • onUnregister

      default void onUnregister()
      The type was unregistered, by its owner or because the owning plugin is disabling. Previews still showing have been stopped; anything else the type keeps up, such as worn items, should be undone here.
